links.outcome: Test-retest reproducibility of LLM helmet-status classification across 5 new chat sessions and days
links.effect: LLM did not perfectly replicate analyses across sessions and days (Fleiss κ = 0.91 across 5 trials; P < .001); it consistently replicated its hallucinations.
links.quote: The LLM did not perfectly replicate its analyses across new sessions and days (Fleiss κ = 0.91 across 5 trials; P < .001).

links.outcome: LLM validity versus researcher-reviewed criterion standard
links.effect: High validity compared with the criterion standard (n = 400; κ = 0.98 [95% CI, 0.96-1.00]).
links.quote: It also showed high validity compared with the criterion standard (n = 400; κ = 0.98 [95% CI, 0.96-1.00]).

unlisted_practices: Prompt detail level (low, intermediate, high) effect on LLM information extraction agreement with text string search

screen.reason: The study empirically tests the information extraction performance and reliability/hallucinations of an LLM across different prompt engineering strategies (low, intermediate, high-detail prompts) compared with keyword searches and manual review on unstructured clinical notes.

primary.practice: prompt engineering detail level comparison and test-retest reliability evaluation
